title: Mary, the mother of Jesus
intro: Catholics honor Mary because God chose her to be the mother of Jesus, and Scripture shows her saying yes to God, serving others, and standing at the foot of the cross. We do not worship her; we honor her as the Lord's mother and ask her to pray for us, as we would ask any faithful friend. She always points us to her Son.
phrasings: why do Catholics pray to Mary
what does the Bible say about Mary
is Mary the mother of God

verses.why: The angel greets Mary as full of grace, and she answers with her yes to God.
Elizabeth calls her blessed, and Mary says all generations will call her blessed.
At Cana, Mary brings a need to Jesus and tells the servants to do whatever he says.
From the cross, Jesus gives Mary to his beloved disciple as his mother.
The woman clothed with the sun, an image the Church has long seen as Mary and the Church.

title: The saints and intercession
intro: Catholics ask the saints to pray for us the same way we ask a friend or relative to pray for us. Death does not break the family of Christ, so those in heaven are alive in him and still care for us. Their prayers do not replace Jesus; they join ours to his, the one mediator between God and us.
phrasings: why do Catholics pray to saints
what does the Bible say about saints
are saints in heaven praying for us
what is the communion of saints

verses.why: The elders in heaven offer the prayers of the saints before the Lamb.
We are surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses cheering us on.
The prayer of a righteous person is powerful, and the saints are the most righteous of all.
Moses and Elijah, long gone from earth, appear and speak with Jesus.
Judas Maccabeus sees the late prophet Jeremiah praying for the people.

title: The Eucharist and Holy Communion
intro: At the Last Supper Jesus took bread and said, “This is my body,” and the Church has always taken him at his word. Catholics believe the bread and wine truly become his Body and Blood, so Communion is not only a symbol but real union with Christ. It is the heart of Catholic life, the source and summit of our faith.
phrasings: is communion really the body of Christ
what does the Bible say about the Eucharist
how to live a Eucharistic life

The cup and the bread are a real sharing in Christ's blood and body.
The disciples recognize the risen Jesus in the breaking of the bread.
Jesus promises that whoever comes to him will never hunger.

title: Going to Mass and keeping Sunday
intro: The Mass is where Catholics worship together, hear God's Word, and receive Christ in the Eucharist. Gathering on Sunday, the day of the Resurrection, goes back to the first Christians, and the Church asks us to keep it as a holy day. It is less a rule than a weekly meeting with the Lord and his family.
phrasings: do I have to go to Mass
what does the Bible say about going to church
is it a sin to miss Mass

verses.why: We are told not to neglect meeting together but to encourage one another.
The first Christians gathered for teaching, fellowship, the breaking of the bread, and prayer.
On the first day of the week, the disciples came together to break bread.
The Sabbath is set apart as holy time for God and rest.
Jesus promises to be present wherever two or three gather in his name.

title: Purgatory
intro: Purgatory is the Church's teaching that souls who die in God's friendship but are not yet fully purified are cleansed before entering heaven. It is not a second chance or a lesser hell, but God's mercy finishing the work of love. That is why Catholics pray for the dead: love does not end at the grave.

verses.why: Judas offers prayers and sacrifice for fallen soldiers, showing prayer for the dead was practised in Israel.
A person can be saved as through fire after his works are tested.
Jesus speaks of sins forgiven in the age to come.
Nothing unclean will enter heaven, so purification is needed.
Without holiness no one will see the Lord.

title: Peter and the Church's authority
intro: Jesus gave Simon a new name, Peter, meaning rock, and told him he would build his Church on him and give him the keys of the kingdom. Catholics see that role continuing in the pope, the successor of Peter, a visible sign of unity for the whole Church. Authority in the Church is meant for service, as Jesus told Peter: feed my sheep.
phrasings: why do Catholics have a pope
what does the Bible say about Peter

Jesus asks Peter three times to feed and tend his sheep.

At the Council of Jerusalem, Peter speaks and the assembly falls silent.
The Church is called the pillar and foundation of the truth.

title: The Rosary and devotions
intro: The Rosary is a simple way of praying with Scripture. We repeat familiar prayers while meditating on the life of Jesus through the eyes of Mary, which quiets the mind and keeps the heart on Christ. The Hail Mary itself is made of Gospel words: the angel's greeting and Elizabeth's blessing.

verses.why: The angel's greeting is the first half of the Hail Mary.
Elizabeth's blessing is the second half.
Jesus gives us the Our Father, which opens every decade.
Praying a repeated refrain has deep roots in the Psalms.
Mary treasured these things in her heart, which is what the Rosary invites us to do.

title: Catholic and Protestant differences
intro: Catholics and Protestants share faith in Jesus, the Trinity, and the Bible, but differ on Church authority, the sacraments, Mary and the saints, and the role of Tradition. Catholics hold that God's Word comes through both Scripture and the apostolic Tradition of the Church. The Church recognizes all baptized Christians as brothers and sisters and prays for unity.

verses.why: Paul tells believers to hold to the traditions taught by word or by letter.
John says Jesus did many things that are not written in his Gospel.
Scripture is inspired and useful for teaching and training.
There is one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith.
Jesus prays that all believers may be one.

title: The seven sacraments
intro: The sacraments are seven gifts through which Christ is truly present and acts in our lives: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Reconciliation, Anointing of the Sick, Holy Orders, and Matrimony. Each uses an outward sign such as water, oil, bread, or words to give an inward grace. Jesus gave them to his Church so that his love would reach us in real, tangible ways.
phrasings: how to live a sacramental life

verses.why: Baptism: to be born of water and the Spirit.
Confirmation: the apostles lay hands and the Spirit is received.
Eucharist: eating his flesh and drinking his blood.
Reconciliation: Jesus gives the apostles authority to forgive sins.
Anointing of the Sick: the elders anoint and pray for the sick.
Holy Orders: the apostles lay hands on those chosen to serve.
Matrimony: marriage is a great mystery, a sign of Christ and the Church.

title: Angels and guardian angels
intro: Angels are real spiritual beings who serve God and carry out his plans, and the Church teaches that each of us has a guardian angel. They appear throughout Scripture as messengers, protectors, and worshippers. Catholics ask for their help, especially the archangels Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael, while worship belongs to God alone.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about angels

verses.why: God commands his angels to guard you in all your ways.
Jesus says the angels of little ones always see the Father's face.
Angels are ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.

Raphael says he is one of the seven angels who stand before the Lord.

title: Demons and spiritual warfare
intro: Scripture takes evil seriously without making us afraid of it: the devil is real, but Christ has already conquered him. The Church's answer is simple: stay close to the sacraments, pray, read Scripture, and trust in God's protection. We resist through faith, not through fear or fascination.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about demons

verses.why: Put on the armour of God to stand against evil.
Stay alert, because the devil prowls; resist him, firm in faith.
Submit to God, resist the devil, and he will flee.
Jesus gives his disciples authority over the enemy.
Jesus defeats temptation by answering with Scripture.

title: The end times and the Second Coming
intro: Scripture tells us Christ will return in glory, but not when. Jesus warned that no one knows the day or hour, so the call is to live ready and watchful, not to predict dates. The Church teaches that Christ will come to judge the living and the dead and to make all things new.
phrasings: what does the Bible say about the end times
signs of the end of the world

verses.why: No one knows the day or the hour, so stay ready.
The angels promise that Jesus will return in the same way he left.
Christ says he is coming soon and is the Alpha and the Omega.
The day comes like a thief, so live as children of the light.
With the Lord a day is like a thousand years; he is patient, wanting all to repent.

title: Creation and evolution
intro: The Church teaches that God created everything out of love and that human beings are made in his image. The Bible tells us who made the world and why, not the scientific details of how, so Catholics can accept the findings of science, including evolution, without giving up faith in a Creator. Faith and reason are meant to work together.
phrasings: what does Genesis say about creation
how did God create the world

verses.why: God creates all things and calls them good.
God forms man and breathes life into him.
The heavens declare the glory of God.
The earth is full of God's works, all made in wisdom.
All things were made through the Word.

title: The Ten Commandments
intro: The Ten Commandments are God's gift to show us how to love him and our neighbour, not a list of arbitrary rules. Jesus did not cancel them; he fulfilled them and summed them up as love of God and love of neighbour. They remain the foundation of Catholic moral life.

verses.why: God gives the commandments to Moses at Sinai.
Moses repeats them, reminding Israel that God freed them first.
Jesus tells the rich young man to keep the commandments.
Jesus says he came to fulfil the law, not abolish it.
Love is the fulfilment of the law.

title: The Beatitudes and the Sermon on the Mount
intro: The Beatitudes open the Sermon on the Mount and describe what a life of blessing looks like to Jesus: poor in spirit, merciful, pure in heart, peacemakers. They turn the world's idea of success upside down. Catholics see them as a portrait of Christ himself and a map toward holiness.
phrasings: blessed are the poor in spirit

verses.why: The eight Beatitudes.
Luke's shorter version of the blessings.
The Our Father, taught in the same sermon.
Ask, seek, knock, and the Golden Rule.
Build your house on the rock by living his words.

title: Who wrote the Bible and which books belong?
intro: The Bible is a library of 73 books in the Catholic canon, written over centuries by human authors inspired by God. The early Church, guided by the Holy Spirit, discerned which books belong. Catholic Bibles include seven Old Testament books, called the deuterocanon, that many Protestant Bibles omit, such as Wisdom, Sirach, and Maccabees.
phrasings: why does the Catholic Bible have more books
how was the Bible put together

verses.why: All Scripture is inspired by God.
Prophecy came as people were moved by the Holy Spirit.
The word of God is living and active.
Luke explains how he carefully set down his account.
An example of a deuterocanonical book, praising wisdom.

title: How to read the Bible
intro: You do not have to start at Genesis. Many people begin with the Gospel of Mark or John, then Acts and the Psalms, reading a little each day and praying before they begin. Catholics read Scripture within the Church so that the Spirit and Tradition help guide understanding, as Philip did with the Ethiopian official.
phrasings: where should I start reading the Bible
how to read the Bible daily

verses.why: God's word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my path.
Philip helps the Ethiopian understand Isaiah, showing the value of guidance.
Jesus explains how all of Scripture points to him.
Keep God's word on your lips and meditate on it day and night.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.

title: Old Testament laws and violence
intro: Some Old Testament laws and wars are hard to read. The Church teaches that God revealed himself gradually, and that earlier laws belonged to a particular time and people until Christ brought the fullness of revelation. Jesus fulfilled the law, and we read difficult passages in the light of him.
phrasings: why is the Old Testament violent
do Old Testament laws still apply

verses.why: Jesus came not to abolish the law but to fulfil it.
God spoke in many ways, and finally through his Son.
Christ is the goal of the law.
The law was a guardian that led us to Christ.
Ritual laws were a shadow of what was to come.

title: David and Goliath
intro: A young shepherd, armed with a sling and trust in God, faces a giant who terrifies an entire army. David's victory is not about his strength but about God's: the battle belongs to the Lord. The story teaches that the giants in our own lives are never bigger than the God who stands with us.
phrasings: how did David defeat the giant

title: Noah and the flood
intro: God sees the violence on earth and saves Noah's family and the animals through the ark. After the flood he makes a covenant, with the rainbow as its sign, promising never again to destroy the earth by water. The Church sees the ark as an image of salvation and the flood as a sign of Baptism.
phrasings: why did God flood the earth
how many animals on the ark

title: Moses and the Exodus
intro: God hears the cries of his enslaved people and calls Moses from the burning bush to lead them out of Egypt. Through the plagues, the Passover, and the crossing of the sea, Israel learns that the Lord is a God who rescues. The Exodus is the pattern of every later salvation and points to Christ's Passover.

title: The Prodigal Son
intro: A son demands his inheritance, wastes it, and returns in shame, only to be met by a father running to embrace him. Jesus tells this parable to show that God's mercy goes further than our failures. The only question is not whether the Father will welcome us home, but whether we will go.

title: The Good Samaritan
intro: Asked who his neighbour is, Jesus tells of a Samaritan, an outsider, who stops to care for a wounded stranger while religious leaders pass by. A neighbour is anyone in need whom we can help. His closing words to us are simple: go and do likewise.

title: Jonah and God's mercy
intro: Jonah runs from God's call to warn Nineveh, is swallowed by a great fish, and finally obeys. When Nineveh repents, God forgives them, and Jonah is angry. The book is about God's mercy for everyone, even those we think do not deserve it, and Jesus points to the sign of Jonah as a sign of his Resurrection.
phrasings: story of Jonah and the whale

title: The story of Job
intro: Job loses everything and suffers terribly, yet remains faithful while asking God hard questions. His friends offer easy explanations; God offers himself. The book teaches that suffering is not always a punishment and that God's wisdom is greater than we can see, and Catholics see Job as a foreshadowing of Christ, the innocent sufferer.

title: Psalms for every moment
intro: The Psalms are the Church's prayer book, with words for every mood: praise, fear, anger, grief, and trust. When you cannot find your own words, they give you words that Jesus himself prayed. Catholics pray them daily, especially in the Liturgy of the Hours.
